summary_paragraph: A young woman with a history of tracheobronchomalacia, tracheostomy, and chronic respiratory conditions was admitted for dyspnea, increased secretions, and chills. Initial evaluation showed leukocytosis and positive blood cultures for Staphylococcus lugdunensis and Staphylococcus epidermidis, resistant to oxacillin. Chest X-ray and fiberoptic laryngoscopy were unremarkable, ruling out pneumonia and tracheitis. An echocardiogram showed no endocarditis. Given the high virulence of the organism and its association with her port, the decision was made to remove the port and place a PICC line for continued IV vancomycin. She remained afebrile and hemodynamically stable, with one episode of agitation managed with Ativan. Her hemoglobin remained stable despite chronic microcytic anemia, and she was discharged home with a two-week course of IV antibiotics and plans for outpatient hematology follow-up.
